tsk_01M4TY6209KNWK.title: Implement the pure game engine in src/game/engine.ts
tsk_01M4TY6209KNWK.action: Write src/game/engine.ts exporting exactly Status, Cell, Revealed, Game, Options, DIFFICULTIES (beginner 9x9/10, intermediate 16x16/40, expert 16x30/99), createGame, reveal, toggleFlag, chord, minesLeft. Keep it pure: no DOM, no window, no timers, no Date; the only randomness is a seeded PRNG (e.g. mulberry32) owned by the module and driven by Options.seed. Enforce: rows/cols integers 5-50 and mines 1..rows*cols-9 else createGame throws RangeError; with layout the board is fixed from the start with adjacent precomputed and size rule still enforced; without layout, createGame returns a ready game with every cell mine:false, adjacent:0 and reveal() defers mine placement to the first call, placing exactly mines never on the revealed cell or its neighbours, deterministically when seeded; immutability with no-op calls (reveal of revealed/flagged, toggleFlag on revealed, chord that does not qualify, any call after won/lost) returning the exact same Game reference via early return before cloning; flood fill over zero cells and bordering numbered cells never revealing flagged cells, with lastRevealed distances counting steps only while passing through revealed zero cells (numbered border cells take the distance of the zero cell they attach to); loss reveals every mine and keeps flags; win when every non-mine cell is revealed (flags not required) and then flags every mine; chord on a revealed cell whose number equals flagged-neighbour count reveals hidden unflagged neighbours exactly as reveal would (so an unflagged mine among them loses the game), lastRevealed measured from the chorded cell which is distance 0 but not itself listed as newly revealed; minesLeft = mines minus flags, possibly negative.
tsk_01M4TY6209KNWK.motivation: Delivers the section-2 contract and closes the determinism testability trap (fnd_01M4TXQJXRZPVM, fnd_01M4TXX6DRNGKJ), the deferred first-click placement constraint (fnd_01M4TXPG39BM6M, fnd_01M4TXSVHNRTM6), lastRevealed distance semantics (fnd_01M4TXPG39GW2Q, fnd_01M4TXSVHNTCHH), same-reference no-op identity (fnd_01M4TXPG39B6G2), chord wrong-flag loss (fnd_01M4TXPG39WZQ4), win-flags-all-mines (fnd_01M4TXPG392Z3V), and the engine/DOM seam (fnd_01M4TXTK8DNA5A).

tsk_01M4TY6209XCBX.action: Implement the browser layer importing the engine, split into small modules: src/ui/board.ts (renders #board as role=grid with one role=row per row of <button role=gridcell> cells carrying data-row/data-col/data-state, number text for adjacent>0, aria-labels stating position and state like 'Row 3, column 5, hidden' / 'revealed, 2 adjacent mines', data-exploded on the losing mine, wrong-flag state after loss; mouse: left click reveals, right click flags with contextmenu suppressed, left click on a revealed number chords; keyboard roving tabindex — exactly one cell tabindex=0, arrows move focus clamped at edges, Enter/Space reveal or chord, F flags, visible focus outline), src/ui/sound.ts (Web Audio synthesis only, no audio files: distinct tones for single reveal, cascade, flag on/off, chord, explosion, and a win melody of at least 3 notes; lazily create the AudioContext on the first user gesture; mute gate so nothing starts while muted), src/ui/timer.ts (takes a clock function parameter; whole seconds since first reveal, 0 before, stops at game end, capped at 999), src/ui/persist.ts (localStorage for difficulty choice, per-board best times keyed by difficulty and ?board value, mute state — unmuted by default), src/ui/params.ts (parse ?board= rows of * and . into the layout option via a shared pure helper, ?seed= integer, else remembered difficulty with beginner first). Gate every animation behind @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { * { animation: none !important; transition: none !important } } and skip Web Animations API calls when matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches. Ensure number colors meet 4.5:1 contrast and cells are at least ~24px.

messages.content: Key build-tooling risk identified: file:// self-containment (spec §1) requires inlined JS/CSS, which default Vite build does not provide. Must use vite-plugin-singlefile or equivalent. This is the highest-risk item for the `npm run check` gate passing but the actual contract failing. Recommend verifying dist/index.html loads via file:// as part of the e2e suite.

requirements.quote: TypeScript in strict mode, built with Vite, unit-tested with Vitest, end-to-end tested with Playwright, linted with ESLint.
**No runtime dependencies.** `package.json` may have `devDependencies` only; the shipped game is your own code.
`npm run build` | type-checks, then writes the static site to `dist/`
`npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` (or equivalent)
`npm run lint` | ESLint over the source and tests, no warnings allowed
`npm test` | the unit tests, once (not watch mode)
`npm run test:e2e` | the Playwright tests, against the production build
`npm run check` | typecheck, lint, test and build, stopping at the first failure

opening `dist/index.html` straight from disk (double-clicked, a `file://` address, no server at all) gives a playable game. A browser refuses to load separate script or style files for a page opened that way, so they belong inside the page.
The built site must also work from **any path** on a static server — at `/` and at a sub-path such as `/games/minesweeper/` — so any asset URLs are relative.
Pure logic: no DOM, no timers, no `Math.random` except as described for `seed`.
**Immutable.** No function changes the `Game` it is given. A call that changes nothing returns the very same object it was given.
`rows` and `cols` are integers from 5 to 50, and `mines` from 1 to `rows × cols − 9`. Anything else makes `createGame` throw a `RangeError`.
With `layout`, the board is exactly that grid: `rows`, `cols` and `mines` come from it (any given are ignored), mines never move, and `adjacent` is set from the start. The size rule still applies.

Without `layout`, mines are placed at the first `reveal`: exactly `mines` of them, never on the revealed cell or any of its neighbours. With a `seed`, the placement depends only on the seed, the board size and the first cell. Until placement every cell has `adjacent: 0` and `mine: false`.

`ready` until the first reveal, then `playing`; `lost` when a mine is revealed; `won` when every non-mine cell is revealed (flags are not needed). Once `won` or `lost`, every function returns the game unchanged.

Revealing a hidden, unflagged cell reveals it. If it has `adjacent: 0`, its neighbours are revealed too, and so on outward ... Flagged cells are never revealed this way. `lastRevealed` lists every cell the call revealed, each with its `distance`: 0 for the clicked cell, otherwise the fewest steps from the clicked cell to it, moving one neighbour at a time and passing only through revealed zero cells. Revealing a revealed or flagged cell changes nothing.
**Loss.** Revealing a mine reveals every mine, and the game is `lost`. Flags stay where they are.
**Win.** When the game is `won`, every mine is flagged.
**Flags.** `toggleFlag` flags or unflags a hidden cell; on a revealed cell it changes nothing. There may be more flags than mines.

**Chord.** `chord` on a revealed cell whose number equals the count of flagged neighbours reveals every hidden, unflagged neighbour, exactly as `reveal` would (flood included, and a wrong flag can lose the game). `lastRevealed` measures `distance` from the chorded cell, which is 0 but not itself newly revealed. Otherwise `chord` changes nothing.
`minesLeft` is `mines` minus the number of flagged cells; it can be negative.
One page, `index.html`. These elements and attributes are the contract:

`#board` | `role="grid"`; contains one `role="row"` per row, each holding one `<button role="gridcell">` per cell; shown as the familiar Minesweeper field -- each row's cells side by side on one line, rows stacked top to bottom, so the cells of a column line up

each cell button | `data-row`, `data-col` (0-based); `data-state` is `hidden`, `flagged`, `revealed`, `mine` (a revealed mine) or `wrong-flag` (after a loss, a flag on a non-mine); the mine that lost the game also has `data-exploded="true"`; a revealed cell with `adjacent > 0` has that number as its text, otherwise no text; an `aria-label` that says the cell's position and state
`#status` | `data-status` is the game's status; its text tells the player what is going on
`#mines-left` | `minesLeft`, as text (`-2` when over-flagged)
`#timer` | whole seconds since the first reveal, as text; `0` before; stops when the game ends; never above `999`
`#new-game` | a button: a fresh game of the same kind (same difficulty, or the same `?board`)
`#difficulty` | a `<select>` with options `beginner`, `intermediate`, `expert`; changing it starts a new game of that size; the choice is remembered across reloads
`#best-time` | the fastest win for the current board, in whole seconds, or `—` (an em dash) if there is none; kept across reloads
`#mute` | a button, `aria-pressed="true"` when muted; muted state is remembered across reloads; unmuted by default
**Mouse:** left click reveals; right click toggles a flag (no browser menu appears); left click on a revealed number chords.

**Keyboard:** the board is one Tab stop — exactly one cell has `tabindex="0"`, the rest `-1`. Arrow keys move focus between cells and stop at the edges. Enter or Space reveals the focused cell, or chords it if it is a revealed number; `F` toggles its flag. Focus is always visible.
**State is immediate.** Cell `data-state`, `#mines-left`, `#status` and the rest change in the same task as the input that changed them — never after an animation.
**Best times** are kept per board: per difficulty, and per `?board` value. A win is recorded when it beats the stored time.

`?board=` fixes the board: rows separated by `,`, each a string of `*` (mine) and `.` (safe) — `?board=*....,.....,.....,.....,.....`. The game uses that layout (rule 3), and `#new-game` starts it again.
`?seed=` with an integer makes a random game repeatable (rule 4), at the current difficulty.
With neither, the board is random at the remembered difficulty (beginner the first time).
Every sound is synthesised with the Web Audio API — no audio files.

Distinct sounds for: revealing one cell, a cascade (one reveal that opens more than one cell), placing a flag, removing a flag, a chord, an explosion (loss), and a win — the win is a short melody of at least three notes.
requirements.not_tested: Per fnd_01M4TXQJXRADFQ/fnd_01M4TXX6DR4XPG, distinct sounds and the >=3-note win melody cannot be reliably asserted in e2e — verifiable only by code review (covered by a DoD review criterion in the page task), an honest gap rather than a fake audio test.

requirements.quote: **No sound before the player acts:** no `AudioContext` is created before the first click or key press on the page.
**Muted means silent:** while muted, no sound starts at all.

**Reveal ripple.** Every newly revealed cell animates in (100–600 ms), starting `distance × step` after the input, with a fixed step of 15–40 ms, so a cascade ripples outward from the click. No cell starts later than 1000 ms after the input.
requirements.not_tested: The ripple start-delay formula (distance x step, 15-40ms step, <=1000ms cap) is timing-internal and not reliably assertable in e2e; animation presence/absence is covered via R48's reduced-motion test and a DoD review criterion on the delay computation.

requirements.quote: **Flag.** Placing a flag animates.
requirements.not_tested: Flag-placement animation presence is inspection-only (Web Animations/CSS), verified by the reduced-motion review criterion rather than an e2e assertion that could flake.

requirements.quote: **Loss.** The exploded mine animates (a flash, a shake), and the other mines appear one after another rather than all at once.
